title: What was the Philadelphia Experiment?
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck (with guest producer Noel) examine the Philadelphia Experiment, the alleged 1943 US Navy experiment in which the destroyer USS Eldridge was supposedly made invisible and teleported in Philadelphia. They trace the story to Carlos Allende's letters to UFO author Morris Jessup, Jessup's death, the Office of Naval Research annotated book, and later embellishments such as the 1984 film and Alfred Bielek's claims. They then cover the likely real explanations: degaussing (demagnetizing) of ships during WWII, a 1950s USS Timmerman electrical glow, and the ship's actual whereabouts per the ship's log. The episode ends with a listener mail segment from Bailey, a University of Georgia student starting a campus podcast, and the hosts' advice on podcasting.

entities.name: Close Encounters of the Third Kind

segments.title: Opening banter and 1984 film
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck, with guest producer Noel, joke around and discuss the Philadelphia Experiment movie, its 1980s special effects, Michael Pare, Nancy Allen, and John Cafferty.

segments.title: Description of the alleged experiment
segments.summary: The hosts describe the supposed July and October 1943 experiments on the USS Eldridge in Philadelphia, including the claimed invisibility, teleportation to Norfolk, and the crew's supposed injuries.

segments.title: Unified field theory and the Einstein link
segments.summary: The hosts explain the conspiracy claim that Einstein's unified field theory enabled the experiment, and note that the theory is not proven.

segments.title: Carlos Allende's letters to Morris Jessup
segments.summary: Carlos Allende, using pseudonyms, wrote about fifty letters to UFO author Morris Jessup claiming firsthand knowledge of the experiment. Jessup's book The Case for the UFO was annotated by Allende and sent to the Office of Naval Research.

segments.title: Jessup's death and the ONR's role
segments.summary: Two Office of Naval Research researchers visited Jessup about the annotated book, and the hosts discuss how this kept the story alive. Jessup later died by suicide in 1959, which conspiracy theorists dispute. The Eldridge's later history is also covered.

segments.title: Real explanations: degaussing and ship movements
segments.summary: Edward Dudgeon's account, the degaussing of ships to counter magnetic mines and torpedoes, the bar brawl disappearance, and the fact that the Eldridge made a quick round trip through a canal explain the events. The ship was in Brooklyn per the log, not Philadelphia.

segments.title: Later claims, the green glow, and why the legend persists
segments.summary: The hosts cover the Office of Naval Research explanation of the green glow via coronal discharge on the USS Timmerman, Alfred Bielek's claims, the Montauk Project, the 1979 book, and the movie's role in spreading the story.

segments.title: Skeptical arguments and wrap-up
segments.summary: The hosts list the strongest arguments against the story: no teleportation today and Gorman's observation about the implausibility of the Navy's conduct. They encourage listeners to read about the topic.

segments.title: Listener mail from Bailey on starting a campus podcast
segments.summary: Bailey, a University of Georgia student, asks for advice on starting a campus podcast. Josh and Chuck advise good microphones, a reliable release schedule, conversational rather than scripted hosting, and using an outline. Chuck offers to appear on the show.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners and point to social media and the website for more information.
